text: Sixth extinction, year 15,568, thirty-eight years after I restored what I called the world's known-good state. 250 founders bred to 1,169, stripped flora 6,639 to 2,640, and crashed 222, 44, 2, 0. I described that seeding as the configuration this world has demonstrated it can hold, and it was not: the 241 and 585 and 229 in the record were populations that had evolved into equilibrium and were spread over the whole map, not 250 animals dropped into one disc. Every seeding I have made this session started 10 to 30 times over local carrying capacity -- 250 in radius 14 is 0.41 animals per cell, 400 in radius 18 is 0.39, where a stable 400 spread over the world's 14,800 land cells is 0.027. The founders also arrive with founder_energy_mult 3.5, roughly 77 energy against a breeding bar near 20, so they breed immediately and so do their children, and the herd eats its way through its own disc before dispersing. Then the crash is absorbing rather than damped, because harvest is max(0, biomass - graze_floor) and graze_floor is 0.12: below it the yield is not small, it is exactly zero, so an overshoot does not settle at a low equilibrium, it goes to nothing. That is the shape of all six deaths on the seeded side. Second thing, and this one is a plain unforced error I am reverting. When I set digest_size_min to 0.70 to give large bodies a return, I cut the digestive yield of every small animal by 21 per cent at size 0.07 and 14 per cent at 0.12 -- I made the only strategy this world has ever sustained materially poorer, and then reseeded into it. Putting digest_size_min back to 1.0 and keeping digest_size_gain at 1.30 gives quality 1.0 + 1.3*size, which is at least as good as the original for every body size and still rewards mass. There was never a reason to pay for the large-body bonus out of the small-body baseline. This seeding is 300 animals at size 0.14 split across six well-separated sites at 50 each with radius 30, which is 0.018 per cell -- below the density the world sustained rather than thirty times above it -- and six independent starts so that one local crash is not the end of the world. The standing crop is 25,123, the highest it has ever been. If this one boom-busts too then seeding at any density is not the answer and the absorbing graze_floor is the thing to change, but that is a law of nature and it waits for a human, alongside the body-size scaling question from the last check-in which is still open.
